summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for dizziness, worsening headache, and melena with a significant drop in hemoglobin from 37.5 to 25.5. Evaluation revealed guaiac-positive stool and a history of chronic GVHD, long-term steroid use, and anticoagulation with enoxaparin. CT head showed no acute intracranial process. EGD revealed duodenal erosions with recent bleeding, and colonoscopy showed a sigmoid ulcer and diverticulosis. Capsule endoscopy did not identify an active bleed. H. pylori infection was confirmed, and treatment with amoxicillin and clarithromycin was initiated. Enoxaparin was held during acute bleeding and restarted at a reduced dose of 40 mg daily prior to discharge. Hemoglobin improved to 10.5, and the patient was discharged home with plans for follow-up on pending biopsies, sirolimus level, and platelet function studies.
